exculpate

/EK-skul-payt/ - the stress falls on EK · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Exculpate means to free someone from guilt or blame.

Three independent witnesses placed the peddler two counties away, and their sworn statements exculpated him before the assizes even convened.

Example

Suspicion for the poisoned well fell on the town's unpopular herbalist until the new physician traced the sickness to a cracked cistern; his report exculpated her so thoroughly that the council paid to reglaze the shop windows her neighbors had broken.

Exculpate is built on culpa, 'blame': to exculpate is to pull someone out from under blame, usually by evidence. It is narrower than absolve — a panel can absolve you of a duty, but it is proof that exculpates you of a suspected wrong.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

absolve: Absolve is the ceremonial member of the clearing family: a priest, a panel, or a court declares the burden lifted, and it can cover duties and debts as well as guilt. Exculpate is narrower and colder — it is proof that exculpates, evidence pulling a suspect out from under blame.

acquit: Acquit is the jury's formal not-guilty at the end of a trial — a verdict that the charge was not proven, delivered in a courtroom. Exculpate needs no courtroom at all: an alibi or a dated receipt can exculpate a suspect before charges are ever drawn up.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

incriminate: to point the evidence at someone

accuse: to name them as the wrongdoer

Where it sits · how formally the blame is removed

defend → clear → exculpate

defend vs. exculpate: A lawyer defends a client whether or not the proof favors her; defend stops far short of exculpate, which means the blame is actually lifted.

clear vs. exculpate: To clear a name is the everyday phrase for the same rescue; clear stops just short of exculpate, the formal word for blame removed by proof.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ex-: out, out from

Root — culp: blame, fault

Suffix — -ate: to make, to do

Put it together: Ex- (out) + culp (blame) + -ate (to make) = to take out of blame. Latin culpa, 'fault,' survives wherever English points fingers — the culprit is the one at fault — and exculpate runs the arrow backward, lifting the fault away.

Word Choice

formal / legal

Exculpate is the evidence-room member of this unit's clearing family: documents, alibis, and records exculpate. Boards exonerate, authorities absolve, and events vindicate — reach for exculpate when the proof itself does the lifting.
